blocks.text: A technician opens a flat-pack compressor kit and cannot tell whether the bearing goes in before or after the end cap. A single exploded view with numbered balloons would have told her in five seconds.

blocks.markdown: An **exploded view** is a pictorial assembly drawing in which the parts are pulled apart along their assembly axes, in the order and direction they go together. It communicates the **assembly sequence** without words. Parts that belong on the same axis are separated along that axis, spaced evenly, and linked by thin **centre lines** showing where each part will end up. Standard parts such as screws are drawn with their own line of travel.

blocks.title: Exploded view
blocks.text: A drawing that separates the components of an assembly along assembly axes, keeping their relative orientation, so each part and its place in the sequence can be seen. Alignment is shown by thin chain or centre lines; the first part to assemble is placed deepest.

blocks.markdown: **Balloons and part numbers.** Each part in the assembly drawing is identified by a circle (balloon) with a leader line pointing at the part and an **item number** that matches a line of the bill of materials. Good practice: balloons placed outside the view in rows or columns; leaders never cross; numbers read in sequence; identical parts carry the same item number.

rows: Keep parts on the assembly axis, even spacing
Thin line from part to its final position
Circle outside the view, leader to part
blocks.caption: Elements of an exploded assembly drawing

blocks.markdown: **Simple motion check.** For a moving assembly, check through the full range of motion that parts do not collide. Take a crank-slider: crank of radius $r$, connecting rod of length $l$, slider pin position $x$ measured along the line of travel from the crank axis. For crank angle $\theta$:

blocks.caption: Slider position for crank radius r and rod length l (both in mm); theta is the crank angle from the line of travel

blocks.markdown: At $\theta = 0$ the slider is at its outer limit $x = l + r$; at $\theta = 180^\circ$ it is at its inner limit $x = l - r$. The stroke is therefore $2r$.

blocks.title: Positions of a crank-slider
blocks.prompt: A crank-slider has r = 40 mm and l = 140 mm. Find x at crank angles 0, 90 and 180 degrees and the stroke.

steps.text: At 0 degrees both cos = 1 and sin = 0.
Stroke is the difference of the extremes.

blocks.title: A collision at the end of travel
blocks.prompt: In the same mechanism the slider crown extends 12 mm beyond the pin, and the housing end wall is 185 mm from the crank axis. Does the slider collide?

steps.text: The crown is furthest out when the pin is at its outer limit.
Compare with the wall at 185 mm: 192 > 185.

blocks.answer: Yes: the crown would penetrate the wall by 7 mm at the outer limit; the housing or the stroke must change.

blocks.title: Check the whole range
blocks.text: A collision may occur only at a mid-travel angle, where a rod edge passes a boss, so animating or stepping the crank through 360 degrees is essential. Checking only the two end positions is not enough.

items: Identify the assembly axes and the order of assembly.
Separate parts along each axis, in sequence.
Add centre lines linking each part to its position.
Add balloons outside the view, numbered to the BOM.
For moving parts, step through the full range and test for interference.

points: An exploded view separates parts along assembly axes to show sequence and alignment.
Balloons carry item numbers that match the bill of materials, with identical parts sharing one number.
A crank-slider has stroke 2r; check for collisions through the whole range, not only at the ends.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the thin centre lines drawn between parts in an exploded view?

options.text: To show the dimensions of the parts
To show how each part aligns with its assembly axis

questions.correctOptionText: To show how each part aligns with its assembly axis

distractorRationale.c: Section planes use chain lines with arrows.

questions.explanation: These lines link each part to its final position along the assembly axis. They carry no size and are not section or hidden lines.

questions.stem: A balloon on an assembly drawing contains the number 4. What does the 4 refer to?

options.text: The item number of a line in the bill of materials

questions.correctOptionText: The item number of a line in the bill of materials

distractorRationale.c: Sheet number is in the title block.
distractorRationale.d: Scale is in the title block.

questions.explanation: The balloon key is the BOM item number. The quantity is a separate BOM column.

questions.stem: A crank-slider has crank radius 30 mm and connecting rod length 110 mm. Calculate the stroke of the slider in mm.
questions.explanation: Outer limit l + r = 140 mm, inner limit l - r = 80 mm, difference 60 mm = 2r. The rod length cancels.

questions.stem: For a crank radius of 25 mm and rod length 100 mm, calculate the slider position x at a crank angle of 90 degrees, in mm, from the crank axis.
questions.explanation: At 90 degrees x = sqrt(100^2 - 25^2) = sqrt(9375) = 96.82 mm. The cos term is zero at this angle.

questions.stem: A gear, a spacer and a retaining nut are fitted in that functional order onto a shaft, working from the shaft shoulder outward. In the exploded view drawn along the shaft axis, which order do the parts appear from the shoulder outward?

distractorRationale.d: Spacer would be trapped after the nut.

questions.explanation: The exploded view reproduces the assembly order along the axis: the gear seats on the shoulder, the spacer follows, and the nut closes the stack. Any other order cannot be assembled in that sequence.

questions.stem: A crank-slider has r = 35 mm and l = 110 mm. The slider crown projects 8 mm beyond the pin and the housing end wall is 150 mm from the crank axis. What happens at the outer limit?

options.text: No collision, there is 5 mm clearance
The crown hits the wall, overlapping by 3 mm
The crown hits the wall by 8 mm

questions.correctOptionText: The crown hits the wall, overlapping by 3 mm

distractorRationale.c: Uses the projection as the overlap.

questions.explanation: The outer limit of the pin is 110 + 35 = 145 mm, and the crown reaches 153 mm, which is 3 mm past the wall at 150 mm. Checking only the pin position would miss this collision.

questions.stem: A motion study of a crank-slider checks only the two end positions (0 and 180 degrees) and reports no collisions. Why is this insufficient?

options.text: The ends are always the worst case
A collision can occur at an intermediate crank angle where the rod or crank passes a nearby feature
Only the crank angle of 90 degrees matters

questions.correctOptionText: A collision can occur at an intermediate crank angle where the rod or crank passes a nearby feature
questions.explanation: Interference may occur anywhere in the range, for example where the rod sweeps past a boss. Step through the whole cycle.

questions.stem: Describe how to produce an exploded view that shows the assembly sequence of a bearing, shaft and end cap into a housing.
markingGuide: Separate the parts along it in the order of assembly
Thin centre lines linking each part to its position
Fasteners shown on their own lines of travel
questions.explanation: The answer must mention axis, order, spacing and centre lines. Each point in the marking guide earns credit, so state every point explicitly and give its reason.

questions.stem: An assembly drawing has balloon 3 on two different parts, no balloon on a washer that is in the BOM, and leaders that cross. State each fault and the correction.
markingGuide: A balloon number must identify a single part: renumber
Washer needs a balloon and the same item number as the BOM line
Leaders should not cross: reposition balloons
Item numbers must match BOM lines
questions.explanation: Each fault should be paired with a fix that restores a one-to-one link between balloon and BOM line. Each point in the marking guide earns credit, so state every point explicitly and give its reason.

questions.stem: Identical parts in an assembly carry the same item number.
questions.explanation: One item number, one BOM line with a quantity, serves all copies of an identical part. Different parts must carry different numbers.
